data.name: Ferroptosis
data.description: Iron-dependent, lipid-peroxidation-driven regulated cell death that is modulated by mTOR signalling and autophagy.
data.description_beginner: A distinct way for a cell to die: iron inside the cell sets off a chain reaction that shreds the fatty membranes holding it together. It is not the tidy, programmed suicide most cells use, and both mTOR signalling and autophagy change how easily it happens.

studies.title: Forsythoside A Alleviates Hypertensive Nephropathy by Promoting Mitophagy and Inhibiting Ferroptosis via ASCL1-CCNB1/mTOR Pathway.
studies.authors: Cui X; Yang D; Zhang Z; Wang C; Li H; Sun J; Zhang T; Wang M

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

studies.model_system: C57BL/6 mouse; NRK-52E rat kidney cells
studies.finding: Forsythoside A binds ASCL1 and blocks the downstream CCNB1/mTOR axis, promoting mitophagy and suppressing ferroptosis to protect against Ang II-induced hypertensive nephropathy in mice — without lowering blood pressure.
